PullRequest.Title: Add Copy Link to Agent Host chat editor context menus
PullRequest.Body:

Adds **Copy Link** to Agent Host chat editor tab context menus. The copied `agent-host-session://` URL is the same format recognized by rich session/chat pills in Markdown, rather than the editor's UI resource or an external product-launch URL.

- Resolves the invoked editor context, including inactive tabs and multiple selections; copies one unique URL per line.
- Preserves backend identity, connection authority, and peer-chat selection, and waits for pending provisional session identities.
- Reports unavailable/uncreated sessions without changing the clipboard, hides the menu entry when AI features are disabled, and updates accessibility help.
- Adds seven focused regression tests.

No linked issue; this implements a directly requested workflow.

### How to test

1. Open an Agent Host chat in an editor tab and send a message.
2. Right-click its tab and choose **Copy Link**.
3. Use the copied URL in a Markdown link. It should render as a rich session/chat pill on a surface supporting link presentations and open the corresponding chat.
4. Repeat with an inactive tab, several selected tabs, a remote session, and a peer chat.

### Validation

Validation performed before commit; the task files are unchanged:

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\actions\chatCopyActions.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHost\openSessionLinkOpener.contribution.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 13 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\actions\chatCopyActions.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\actions\chatAccessibilityHelp.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\actions\chatCopyActions.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Commit hygiene hook — passed.

Used dbgjs to inspect the existing chat editor tabs and context menu in a running Insiders window. The new menu entry has not been exercised end-to-end in an updated UI build; full type-check, integration, and smoke suites were not run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Copy Link from an Agent Host chat editor tab, including a multi-tab selection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve the invoked editor context, synchronously resolve each session identity, concurrently await any already-running local provisional-session tail, build and deduplicate URLs, then complete one clipboard write. The clipboard write and any awaited pending operation are on the command's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the final deduplicated link text to the native clipboard (or the browser clipboard API on web).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one write per successful command, independent of selected-tab count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Copy Link editor action did not exist, so this workflow made no clipboard call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The command awaits the clipboard write before announcing success.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Await an already-running per-resource provisional Agent Host lifecycle operation, which may itself be dispatching, creating, or disposing a session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one observed coalesced pending tail per selected ambient-host resource; the action initiates zero Agent Host calls, and stable resources return immediately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no Copy Link command path; the underlying provisional operations and their per-resource coalescing pre-existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: If provisional identity creation is already in flight, the command waits so it can copy the authoritative backend identity; selected resources are awaited concurrently.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective cardinality is the number of selected ChatEditorInput tabs; normally one and at most the user's currently selected open tabs. URL construction scales linearly with selected tabs and URI length; duplicate output URLs are collapsed before the single clipboard write.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Promise.all concurrently processes selected tabs. It does not create Agent Host operations: waitForPending only observes the per-resource coalesced tail already stored by the provisional service. One clipboard write occurs after all selected tabs settle.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session identities are resolved from in-memory maps/policies. waitForPending reads the per-resource pending map and returns immediately on the common warm/stable path; concurrent provisional lifecycle work is already coalesced by SequencerByKey. There is no new positive or negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed command, Promise.all fan-out, pending-map behavior, synchronous identity lookup, and one clipboard boundary were traced directly. No new Agent Host boundary call is scheduled by the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously selected tabs and frequency of invoking Copy Link during an in-flight provisional operation are uncertain, but both are user-bounded. Clipboard latency is platform-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Per-tab CPU/allocation is small and user-bounded, pending work is observed rather than duplicated, and expensive output is coalesced into one clipboard operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open chat accessibility help for panel, edits, or agent views
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On explicit accessibility-help invocation, append one localized static sentence to the existing content array, join/render the help text through the existing accessible-view provider. No filesystem, subprocess, IPC, database, or network work is introduced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant additional work: one localized string and one array entry per help invocation, independent of transcript or session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single invocation on the existing accessibility-help path; no queue or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache or retained lifecycle. The generated string lives with the existing provider for that help view.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed branch and provider call path are direct and contain no expensive boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the added work is constant and only runs when help is explicitly requested.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the constant string allocation is negligible and off startup/render hot paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench contribution registration and editor-tab context-menu evaluation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At chat contribution module initialization, register one additional Action2 descriptor. When an editor title context menu is assembled, evaluate three context-key predicates; action services and session resolution are accessed only after explicit invocation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant registration cost and constant predicate evaluation per relevant context-menu construction; independent of open-session history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous metadata registration/menu evaluation with no asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache added or invalidated. The provisional service remains delayed and is fetched only in run(). Its module was already transitively imported by the existing chat contribution through chatSlashCommands.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registration and import paths were traced, including the pre-existing import of the provisional service module.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact menu-open frequency varies, but changed work is constant and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No eager-work or startup regression: the diff registers metadata but does not instantiate the delayed Agent Host service or cross an expensive boundary until the user invokes the command.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and all diff pages. Traced command invocation, multi-selection scaling, provisional-session waiting/coalescing, clipboard boundaries, accessibility-help generation, and startup/menu registration. No high-confidence diff-caused performance issue met the reporting threshold.
